headline: Curriculum Committee reviewed VTCAP test data, the teaching and learning plan, and universal screener implementation; no votes were recorded.
summary: The committee reviewed district VTCAP proficiency data, noting ELA at 58% and math at 42%, with gaps between FRL and non-FRL students. Members discussed the three-year teaching and learning plan, external support providers, and K-3 universal screening required under Act 139, then outlined next steps including meetings in early October and presenting the plan to teachers before it goes to the board.
plain_text:
Curriculum Committee Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, September 22, 2026 at 4:00 PM 
Central Office, 150 Colchester Avenue, Conference Room 1G 
Present: Matthew Price, Gary Golden, Tom Flanagan, Katherine Grykien, Heather Amato 
 
 
1. Opening  
1.1 Call meeting to order  
4:05pm  
1.2 Suspend Robert's Rules 
 
2. Public Comment 
None 
 
3. Discussion  
3.1 VTCAP Data Review 
 District ELA at 58%, math at 42%, both up 2-3 points from prior year. Data indicate 
that this is moving in the right direction from year to year.  
 Data have stayed within a 2-4 point band for the last 3 years.  
o Big year-over-year swings warrant scrutiny; 2-3 point moves are normal, 5-
10 points would be exceptional. 
 Grade 4 drove ELA gains; all other grades saw net decreases in proficient students. 
o This increase is meaningful given that this cohort was much lower than 
prior cohorts in grade 3.  
 A significant gap persists between FRL and non-FRL students; the district is 57% 
free and reduced lunch. 
o The district has a 48-point gap in English and a 47-point gap in math.   
o The gap is attributed to inconsistent grade-level instruction, siloed 
supports, and insufficient intervention for students needing more. 
 Global majority and special education gaps also exist, though they are smaller 
than the FRL and non-FRL gap. 
 Some schools have shown bright spots (73-80% proficient), which is credited to 
veteran teams and strong MTSS.  
3.2 Teaching & Learning Plan Review 
 Three priorities: strengthen tier-one instruction, build responsive MTSS (including 
student support and multilingual), grow educator and leadership capacity. 
 External support from Stern Center, All Learners Network (K-8 math), Teacher 
Development Group (HS math), and Sawmill Brook Consulting for ILT teaming. 
Page 1 of 2
Draft
 Illustrative Math adoption underway; literacy coherence work continued from last 
year; HS and MS building curriculum maps. 
 AI guidance still in development via internal work group and a national district 
cohort; policy not yet finalized.  
3.3 Universal Screener & MTSS 
 District adopted an approved universal screener this year, K-3 literacy, currently 
mid-window. The screener is being given K-11 in math and literacy. The systematic 
response is in K-3 literacy as required by law (Act 139) 
 State law requires K-3 screening three times per year starting next year. 
o Kindergarten will be excluded in the fall because students are newly in the 
district.  State will require Kindergarten to be screened in the fla  starting 
next school year (27-28) 
 The screener enables systematic identification of students who need support 
rather than relying on individual teacher judgment.  
3.4 Next Steps 
 Work with Lauren, Katherine, Nina, and Bindu in early October to define artifacts 
and benchmarks for measuring plan implementation. 
 Reconvene school teams on October 7 to run the screening process together under 
Act 139. 
 Present the three-year teaching and learning plan to teachers before it goes to the 
board. 
 Bring HS-specific attention to common curriculum and assessments to avoid 
stalling like prior proficiency-based effort. 
 Finalize AI guidance from the internal work group once outstanding technical 
questions are resolved.  
4. Adjournment
